text_blocks.snippet: High blood pressure (hypertension) usually has no symptoms at all, which is why doctors call it the "silent killer".

list.snippet: No warning signs: Most people with high blood pressure feel completely fine.
Silent progression: You can have high blood pressure for years without knowing it.
Regular checks: The only way to know your numbers is to measure your blood pressure with a cuff.

text_blocks.snippet: When blood pressure rises to dangerously high levels (above 180/120 mm Hg), it can cause a medical emergency. Seek immediate care if high readings happen with these symptoms:

list.snippet: Severe headache: A sudden, very painful head throbbing.
Chest pain: Tightness or squeezing in the chest area.
Shortness of breath: Trouble catching your breath while resting or moving.
Vision changes: Blurry vision, double vision, or sudden vision loss.
Neurological signs: Sudden weakness, numbness, confusion, or trouble speaking.

text_blocks.snippet: You can learn more about risk factors on the American Heart Association or check the detailed overview from the Cleveland Clinic.
